label: rem:surreal-squeeze-interpretation
title: Interpretation: cost dominates budget, and the downstream bounds
html:
The "cost" of a standard-scale deviation \delta from the classical configuration — whether a zero off the critical line, a singular spike in the velocity gradient, or a non-trivial Collatz orbit — is \delta^2 \cdot \Omega_q \asymp \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1}. The "budget" available from the mass-gap dissipation is \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3. The surreal squeeze states that the cost strictly exceeds the budget. No passage to the limit is needed: the inequality is already exact in the ordered field.

Downstream. Every millennium-problem remark in this chapter and Chapter 7 (fluid dynamics) reduces to this lemma. See:

  • Navier--Stokes surreal bound;
